name: Apple Cider Brined Turkey
description: An 11–12 lb turkey brined overnight in apple cider, citrus, and herbs, then roasted.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 cups kosher salt (Diamond Crystal, or 3/4 cup Morton)

recipeInstructions.text: Don't brine a kosher, self-basting, or "enhanced" turkey; it's already salted. A frozen bird needs about 3 days in the fridge to thaw.

In a large pot, bring water to a simmer with kosher salt, brown sugar, black peppercorns, allspice berries, bay leaves, fresh rosemary, fresh thyme, and fresh sage. Stir until the salt and sugar dissolve, then take it off the heat.
Add water and apple cider. Stir in orange, lemon, apple, yellow onion, garlic, carrots, and celery. Chill until fully cold.
Remove the neck and giblets from the turkey and save them for the gravy. Submerge the turkey in the cold brine in a brining bag or 5-gallon bucket and refrigerate 12-18 hours.
Lift the turkey out, discard the brine, and pat it very dry. For crisp skin, leave it uncovered in the fridge for a few hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 325°F. Scatter yellow onion, carrot, and celery in a roasting pan with a rack, add chicken stock, and set the turkey on the rack.
Roast until the thickest part of the breast reads 160°F and the thigh 175°F, 2 1/2-3 hours. Add a splash of water if the pan goes dry. Tent with foil and rest 30-40 minutes while you make the gravy.
Brining makes the drippings salty, so season the gravy only after tasting.
